roads.name: Summit Road
words: Curve after curve after curve: 58 in 3.6 miles, about 16 a mile.
Plenty of tight curves among them.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 1,605 to 2,310 ft, with 1,019 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 25 mph limit its corners still ask for about 0.29 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace.

roads.name: North Castle Hot Springs Road
words: Properly twisty: 22 curves in 2.6 miles, about 8 a mile.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 2,639 to 3,022 ft, with 516 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 55 mph limit its corners still ask for about 1.03 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this assumes 55 mph.

roads.name: Wickenburg–Kingman Highway
words: Sweeping and steady: 10 curves in 3.6 miles.
Tight and technical: most curves turn on a radius under 130 ft.
From 2,092 to 2,370 ft, with 308 ft of up and down along the way.
6 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
